status: draft - eligibility revision; formulas identical to 2.0.0-draft.3, which scripts/extract_features_v2.py implements and loads from configs/feature_spec_v2.json

changes: active=false (with inactive_since reason) for login_failed_count, download_command_lines, unique_command_names, input_line_max_bytes, input_bytes_total. Definitions, formulas, dtypes and output columns unchanged.

Active (model input) features, in specification order: login_success, session_duration_s, input_line_count, shell_operator_lines, time_to_first_input_s, inter_input_mean_s, inter_input_std_s, tty_output_bytes.
Written as a new file (configs/feature_spec_v2_draft4.json) because the unchanged extractor requires draft.3 at configs/feature_spec_v2.json; that file is kept byte-identical.

Descriptive coverage only: provenance class file_event_network_download_failed and descriptive field download_failed_events for cowrie.session.file_download.failed (observed in the 2026-11-10 smoke test; emitted by Cowrie's wget.py and curl.py error handlers).
url_download_events clarified: counts successful downloads (cowrie.session.file_download with 'url') only; failed attempts and local redirect writes are separate.
forbidden_inputs extended with the generator's diagnostic terminal output and per-command manifest fields.
No model feature added, removed or redefined; the 13 model features and their statuses are unchanged.

Conditional count clarified: draft.1 marked 5 individual features as conditional or leakage-checked (earlier summaries said 'four', which was a miscount). draft.2 has 7 conditional features in 4 groups and 6 core features.
time_to_first_input_s added to the generator leakage review (group C2): reliable event provenance, but the value can reflect generator or profile timing.
session_duration_s added to the generator leakage review (group C3): command behaviour, blocking emulated commands and timeout handling can create category fingerprints.
inter_input_mean_s and inter_input_std_s defined explicitly as intervals between recorded command.input events, not necessarily client typing intervals.
Recorded-input naming kept unchanged; no feature renamed.
conditional_groups added: risk tested, evidence to retain, failure action, exclusion mechanism.
Every feature now separates event_provenance, availability, statistical_leakage_risk and deployment_domain_compatibility.
feature 'role' replaced by 'status' (core | conditional) and 'conditional_group'; 'provenance' renamed 'event_provenance'; versioning_policy added.

versioning_policy.deactivate_feature: Set the feature's 'active' to false with a dated reason and bump the pre-release/patch revision. Formulas and the output schema do not change; the extractor still computes and writes the column, and only the model input list (features with active = true) changes. No re-extraction is needed.
versioning_policy.change_formula_or_add_feature: Bump the minor version (2.1.0) and re-extract every dataset that uses the specification.
versioning_policy.change_source_event_unit_or_provenance: Bump the major version (3.0.0); results are not comparable across major versions.
versioning_policy.regenerate_data_instead: If a conditional feature fails because of a generator artefact (not because the feature is meaningless), the specification is unchanged; the generator is fixed and the data regenerated, then the check is repeated.

scope.unit: one Cowrie SSH session (one cowrie.session.connect / session id)
scope.telemetry_source: Cowrie JSON event log (cowrie.json) only; no TTY recordings, no manifest, no network capture
scope.in_scope: observable printable command behaviour, authentication outcome, session timing, server terminal output volume
out_of_scope: binary or non-ASCII payload content (Cowrie strips non-ASCII bytes from logged input)
per-attacker or cross-session behaviour (all lab sessions share one relay source IP)
client-specific interpretation of input features (command.input mixes client and Cowrie-executed lines)

assessment_dimensions.event_provenance: Which party produced the events the feature is computed from (client, Cowrie, mixed). Established from Cowrie JSON semantics and the manifest-alignment audit.
assessment_dimensions.availability: Whether the source events exist in a given telemetry source (synthetic V1, real Cowrie).
assessment_dimensions.statistical_leakage_risk: Whether the feature's values in generated training data could reveal the generation profile/category for reasons other than behaviour (generator parameters, templates, constants). Tested by checks L1-L7 on training data only.
assessment_dimensions.deployment_domain_compatibility: Whether the feature's distribution in the isolated lab is expected to resemble real deployment telemetry with the same definition (generator speed, relay, blocked egress, one attempt per connection).

conventions.input_lines: cowrie.command.input events of the session, ordered by timestamp then log order, excluding lines whose stripped text is exactly 'exit' or 'logout'. These are RECORDED lines: they can include lines Cowrie executes itself and can miss client lines; they are not verified client typing.
conventions.line_bytes: len(input.encode('utf-8')) of the logged text, i.e. after Cowrie's own sanitisation
conventions.command_name: first whitespace-separated token of the stripped input line; lines that are empty after stripping are ignored
conventions.missing: NaN in the output; the extractor never imputes. Imputation is a pipeline decision fitted on training data only.
conventions.structural_zero: 0 is used only where the quantity provably cannot occur (e.g. no input lines in a session without a successful login)
conventions.timestamps: ISO-8601 'timestamp' field of each event, parsed as UTC; events sorted by (timestamp, log line order)
conventions.naming: Feature names keep the 'input_' / 'inter_input_' wording for recorded command lines; no name implies verified client provenance.

provenance_classes.connection: session.connect, client.version, client.kex, session.closed: lifecycle; mixed client and server timing
provenance_classes.authentication: login.success, login.failed: client credentials judged by Cowrie
provenance_classes.recorded_command_line: command.input: client-typed lines PLUS lines Cowrie executes itself (scripts run by sh/bash, downloaded files); client lines can also be missing (session closed while a command was blocking). Not client-specific.
provenance_classes.first_recorded_command_line: the first command.input of a session: always client-originated (Cowrie executes nothing before the first client line; 1,498/1,498 aligned live sessions)
provenance_classes.server_emulation: command.failed (one per ';'-separated part; reflects Cowrie's command coverage), session.params, client.size
provenance_classes.server_terminal_output: log.closed.size: bytes Cowrie wrote to the terminal, including the echo of typed input
provenance_classes.file_event_network_download: session.file_download with 'url': a download that Cowrie completed and stored
provenance_classes.file_event_network_download_failed: session.file_download.failed with 'url': Cowrie's emulated wget/curl attempted the URL and failed (DNS failure, unreachable network, refused connection); no file was obtained. In the isolated lab every external download attempt ends here or produces no file event at all.
provenance_classes.file_event_local_redirect: session.file_download with 'destfile' and no 'url' (shell redirect saved by Cowrie; no network)
provenance_classes.file_event_scp_stdin: session.file_download with realm='scp': client lines consumed as scp input, NOT logged as command.input

C1_auth_collinearity.leakage_risk_tested: Redundancy and generator artefact: the lab generator opens one connection per attempt, so the value is 0 or 1 and almost equals 1 - login_success; per-profile 'failed_attempts' settings then appear as session counts, not as this feature.
C1_auth_collinearity.evidence_to_retain: On training data: (a) |Spearman correlation| with login_success < 0.95; (b) L1 and L2 pass; (c) at least one non-lab or pilot sample shows the within-session retry semantics the feature is meant to capture.
C1_auth_collinearity.on_failure: Mark inactive; keep as a descriptive column.

C2_generator_timing.leakage_risk_tested: Profile-specific pacing: profiles_v2*.json give each profile its own delay_range; the generator waits a fixed 0.5/--speed after opening the shell (generate_labelled_traffic.py line 160); --speed rescales all delays. Event provenance of time_to_first_input_s is reliable (client-sent first line), but its value can still be a generator constant or profile parameter. The inter-input features are intervals between recorded command.input events and include Cowrie-executed lines (millisecond gaps) and gaps across lost lines.
C2_generator_timing.evidence_to_retain: (a) Generation metadata shows one category-independent pacing distribution and a fixed --speed for all runs, with wait-for-prompt sending; (b) on training data, L1 and L2 pass (proposed: eta^2 < 0.8, train-range rule and exact-value lookup below agreed thresholds); (c) time_to_first_input_s is not near-constant (coefficient of variation reported) - a near-constant value carries only generator information; (d) L6 reports the share of sessions with Cowrie-executed or missing lines per category, and it is not category-dependent.
C2_generator_timing.on_failure: If (a) fails: fix the generator and regenerate; the specification is unchanged. If (b)-(d) fail with fair generation: mark the failing feature inactive.
C2_generator_timing.exclusion_mechanism: deactivate (patch revision) or regenerate data; no specification regeneration

C3_session_lifecycle.leakage_risk_tested: Category fingerprints from (i) profile-specific command counts multiplied by pacing; (ii) blocking emulated commands (curl/wget/scp) whose run time depends on the lab network (blocked egress) rather than the client; (iii) timeout handling - Cowrie authentication_timeout 120 s and idle_timeout 180 s (cowrie.cfg.dist), and the pre-fix generator's unclosed failed logins (~120 s).
C3_session_lifecycle.evidence_to_retain: On training data: (a) no pre-fix generated sessions included; (b) L1 and L2 pass; (c) the share of sessions within 1 s of 120 s or 180 s is reported per category and is not category-dependent; (d) duration is not mostly explained by category after accounting for input_line_count (reported, e.g. per-category residual summary).
C3_session_lifecycle.on_failure: If caused by generator pacing or timeout artefacts: fix the generator and regenerate. Otherwise mark inactive.
C3_session_lifecycle.exclusion_mechanism: deactivate (patch revision) or regenerate data; no specification regeneration

C4_profile_template_content.leakage_risk_tested: Fixed command templates: a category whose template always (or never) contains pipes, redirections or download commands is revealed by these counts (e.g. download commands only in botnet/exfiltration profiles).
C4_profile_template_content.evidence_to_retain: On training data: (a) L2 eta^2 and exact-value lookup below agreed thresholds; (b) non-zero values occur in at least two categories, including at least one benign profile where realistic; (c) values vary within categories.
C4_profile_template_content.on_failure: Broaden and overlap the profile vocabularies and regenerate; if still failing, mark inactive.
C4_profile_template_content.exclusion_mechanism: deactivate (patch revision) or regenerate data; no specification regeneration

features.name: login_success

statistical_leakage_risk.note: Profiles differ in failed-login share via generator settings; checked by L1/L2.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Same event and meaning in lab and deployment.

features.validation: value in {0,1}; if 1 then at most one login.success event

features.name: login_failed_count
features.definition: Number of rejected authentication attempts within the session
features.missing_policy: never missing (0 is a true count)

statistical_leakage_risk.note: Near-collinear with login_success in generated data; see C1.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Lab: 0 or 1 per session (one attempt per connection). Real clients may retry within one connection.

features.validation: >= 0; flag sessions with login_failed_count = 0 and login_success = 0 (no auth event)

inactive_since.reason: C1 fails: equals 1 - login_success in every Dataset V2 row (Spearman -1.0); no within-session retries (Task 15, Task 16).

features.name: session_duration_s
features.missing_policy: NaN if no cowrie.session.closed (session cut by log rotation or still open)
features.event_provenance: connection (client and server lifecycle; termination cause not distinguishable)

availability.real_cowrie: yes (4,357 of 4,357 unique sessions in train_v1 + eval_v1)

statistical_leakage_risk.note: Command counts x pacing, blocking emulated commands, timeouts; see C3.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Lab duration scales with --speed and blocked egress; deployment durations include human/bot pacing and real timeouts.

features.validation: >= 0; approximately last event time - connect time (tolerance 1 s)

features.name: input_line_count
features.definition: Number of recorded command lines (see conventions.input_lines)
features.missing_policy: never missing; 0 is a true count
features.event_provenance: recorded_command_line (mixed client and Cowrie-executed; client lines can be missing)

statistical_leakage_risk.note: Template length per profile; checked by L1/L2 like every feature.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Same definition; lab loses lines when sending does not wait for the prompt.

features.name: input_bytes_total
features.definition: Total UTF-8 bytes of recorded command lines

statistical_leakage_risk.note: Fixed command strings per profile; L2 exact-value lookup.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Same definition; vocabulary differs from real attackers.

features.validation: >= input_line_count (each non-empty line has >= 1 byte); all bytes ASCII for this Cowrie build (flag otherwise)

inactive_since.reason: Conditional at the Task 16 freeze; user decision 2026-11-11 (Task 17 approval): inactive. Its information beyond input_line_count is command length, the same template-length mechanism as input_line_max_bytes.

features.name: input_line_max_bytes
features.definition: Length of the longest recorded command line
features.event_provenance: recorded_command_line (mixed); a Cowrie-executed script line can be the longest (5,605-char HTML line in train_v1)

statistical_leakage_risk.note: A single long template line can identify a profile; L2.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Same definition; printable payload lengths only.

inactive_since.reason: Strongest command-length template fingerprint: L1 (botnet outside every other range 53%) and L2 lookup 0.71 fail (Task 15, Task 16).

features.name: unique_command_names
features.definition: Number of distinct command names among recorded lines

inactive_since.reason: Deactivated member of the redundant pair with input_line_count (Spearman 0.91); its additional information is template repetition structure (Task 16).

features.name: shell_operator_lines
features.definition: Recorded lines that use a pipe, command separator, redirection or substitution
features.formula: count(line for line in input_lines if any(op in line for op in ['|', ';', '&&', '>', '<', '`', '$(']))

features.name: download_command_lines
features.definition: Recorded lines whose command name is a file-transfer client, regardless of network outcome
features.formula: count(line for line in input_lines if command_name(line) in {'wget','curl','tftp','ftp','ftpget','scp'})

statistical_leakage_risk.note: Download commands appear only in some profiles; see C4.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Counts attempts, which are observable whether or not egress is allowed.

inactive_since.reason: L1/C4 fail after the Task 12 vocabulary redesign: constant 1 in every botnet session; C4 handling 'if still failing -> inactive' (Task 15, Task 16).

features.name: time_to_first_input_s
features.definition: Delay between successful login and the first recorded command line
features.event_provenance: first_recorded_command_line (client-originated in all 1,498 audited sessions; reliable)

availability.synthetic_v1: no (V1 'ackdat' used a different origin and generated offsets)

statistical_leakage_risk.note: Reliable provenance does not prevent leakage: the value can be a generator constant (fixed 0.5/--speed wait) or a profile parameter; see C2.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Lab value is set by the generator's wait and --speed; deployment reflects human or bot behaviour.

features.name: inter_input_mean_s
features.definition: Mean interval between consecutive RECORDED command.input events (not necessarily client typing intervals)
features.event_provenance: recorded_command_line (mixed): intervals between recorded events; Cowrie-executed lines add millisecond gaps and lost client lines merge gaps

statistical_leakage_risk.note: Encodes per-profile delay_range unless generation pacing is category-independent; see C2.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Lab pacing is synthetic and scaled by --speed.

features.validation: gaps computed after sorting by timestamp; flag sessions whose log order and timestamp order disagree (2 such sessions in train_v1)

features.name: inter_input_std_s
features.definition: Population standard deviation of intervals between consecutive RECORDED command.input events (not necessarily client typing intervals)
features.missing_policy: NaN when input_line_count < 3 (fewer than two gaps)
features.event_provenance: recorded_command_line (mixed): intervals between recorded events, as inter_input_mean_s

features.name: tty_output_bytes
features.definition: Bytes Cowrie wrote to the session's terminal
features.missing_policy: 0 when login_success = 0 (no terminal channel exists: structural zero); NaN when login_success = 1 and no log.closed event
features.event_provenance: server_terminal_output (includes echo of typed input; confirmed equal to TTY output bytes in the 2026-11-10 pilot)

availability.synthetic_v1: no (V1 'dbytes' was a per-category random draw)

statistical_leakage_risk.note: Depends on Cowrie's responses to template commands; L2.

deployment_domain_compatibility.note: Same Cowrie build and definition in lab and deployment.

features.validation: >= 0; expected >= input_bytes_total because typed input is echoed; flag otherwise (the only 2 live exceptions are sessions where Cowrie executed a downloaded file, whose lines are not echoed)

feature_counts.note: Core features still pass the general checks L1-L7; 'conditional' marks features with a specific identified risk that needs explicit evidence to retain.

descriptive_fields.name: unknown_command_events
descriptive_fields.reason_not_model: one event per ';' part and per Cowrie-executed line; measures Cowrie's emulation coverage more than behaviour

descriptive_fields.name: url_download_events
descriptive_fields.reason_not_model: successful downloads only; constant 0 expected in the isolated lab (egress blocked); live deployments differ

descriptive_fields.name: download_failed_events
descriptive_fields.reason_not_model: failed download attempts; in the isolated lab their occurrence depends on Cowrie's per-command error handling (wget/curl differ) and on blocked egress, so it is lab-specific

descriptive_fields.name: redirect_write_events
descriptive_fields.reason_not_model: a Cowrie bookkeeping record of a redirect; overlaps shell_operator_lines

descriptive_fields.name: scp_stdin_events
descriptive_fields.reason_not_model: client lines swallowed by emulated scp; reported to quantify input loss

descriptive_fields.name: event_count
descriptive_fields.reason_not_model: dominated by fixed protocol events; redundant

descriptive_fields.name: timestamp_order_mismatch
descriptive_fields.formula: 1 if command.input log order differs from timestamp order

excluded_v1_features.spkts: replaced by input_line_count (V1 omitted failed commands in synthetic data)
excluded_v1_features.dbytes: replaced by tty_output_bytes (V1 synthetic value was injected)
excluded_v1_features.dpkts: count of mixed server/protocol events; baselines differ between generator and Cowrie (4/5 vs 3/6)
excluded_v1_features.rate: (sbytes + dbytes) / dur mixes client input, server output and an artefact-prone duration
excluded_v1_features.sload: derived ratio of input bytes to a duration that includes authentication and idle time
excluded_v1_features.dload: derived from the V1 injected dbytes
excluded_v1_features.tcprtt: SSH handshake time of the lab path (loopback + relay hop), not attacker behaviour
excluded_v1_features.synack: defined as 0.45 * tcprtt; not a measurement
excluded_v1_features.ct_srv_src: collection-size / source-IP count; label leakage in V1, file size in the lab

forbidden_inputs: reserved test markers (e.g. lines starting with 'PILOT_')
generator manifest per-command fields (command_log, auth_log, termination, think_time_s, prompt_match, output_*)

model_input_configuration.note: The frozen configuration is the authoritative model-input list and order. Its record still shows input_bytes_total as 'conditional' (its state at the Task 16 freeze; the file is frozen and was not edited); the approved 2026-11-11 decision makes it inactive here. The model-input list is identical either way.

extraction_compatibility.consequence: All 13 columns are still extracted; datasets extracted under draft.3 are valid under draft.4 without re-extraction.
